title: Scaling Tang's Level-Set Bound to Roots in a Disk of Radius R

problemStatement.formal: For $f(z) = \prod_{i=1}^n (z - z_i)$ with $|z_i| \le R$, let $\Lambda_R(f)$ denote the maximum, over connected components $U$ of $\{z : |f(z)| < 1\}$, of $\operatorname{length}(\partial U)$. Is $\inf_f \Lambda_R(f) = 2R$?
problemStatement.plain: Tang's solution of Erdős #1044 shows that when a polynomial's roots all lie in the unit disk, the sublevel set {|f| < 1} always has a component with boundary longer than 2, and 2 is the sharp infimum. This problem asks whether, when the roots are confined to a disk of radius R instead, the infimum becomes exactly 2R by a scaling argument. The subtlety is that dilating the roots by R multiplies |f| by R^n, so the fixed level {|f| < 1} does not simply rescale, and the proof details may be nontrivial.
whyMatters: Reveals whether Tang's constant 2 is a genuine geometric invariant (the diameter of the region containing the roots) rather than an artifact of the R=1 normalization.

Stress-tests the potential-theoretic picture: {|f|<1} is the negativity region of the logarithmic potential of the roots, and its behavior under dilation is a natural question in quantitative potential theory.
